Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D) normal random variables, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then 

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{n}∼N(n\mu ,\,n{\sigma }^{2}).
$$

Therefore, since ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{18}$ are independent and identically distributed, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{18} & ∼N(18\cdot 1,\,18\cdot {(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(18\cdot 1,\,18\cdot \frac{1}{2}) \\  & =N(18,9).\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to compute the probability $P(16\le Y\le 20).$ We first convert $Y$ into a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(16\le Y\le 20) & =P(\frac{16-18}{\sqrt{9}}\le Z\le \frac{20-18}{\sqrt{9}}) \\  & =P(-\frac{2}{3}\le Z\le \frac{2}{3}) \\  & ≈P(-0.67\le Z\le 0.67) \\  & =1-2P(Z\ge 0.67) \\  & =1-2(1-P(Z\le 0.67)) \\  & =2P(Z\le 0.67))-1 \\  & =2Φ(0.67)-1\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we have

$$
Φ(0.67)=0.7486.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(16\le Y\le 20)=2Φ(0.67)-1=0.4972.
$$
